title: Trip Interruption Allowances and Qualifying Periods, Pass and Trip Protection
content:
Two of the figures a Pass and Trip Protection plan carries answer a lost trip by the day, and two more set how
long a condition must last before a claim on it may be made at all. They are scheduled here across the six
plans.

| Plan | Paid for each day of a trip lost (USD) | Most days of an interrupted trip paid for | Consecutive days the mountain must be shut before a closure claim | Consecutive days certified unfit to ski before a medical claim |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Season Pass Protection Basic | 0.00 | 0 | 0 | 14 |
| Season Pass Protection Plus | 0.00 | 0 | 0 | 10 |
| Season Pass Protection Premier | 0.00 | 0 | 7 | 7 |
| Collective Trip Protection Standard | 185.00 | 7 | 0 | 10 |
| Collective Trip Protection Elite | 345.00 | 10 | 5 | 7 |
| Collective Total Protection Concierge | 650.00 | 21 | 3 | 3 |

**On the daily allowance.** Only the three plans written over trip holdings carry a daily allowance for an
interrupted trip: 185.00 USD for up to 7 days on Collective Trip Protection Standard, 345.00 USD for up to 10
days on Collective Trip Protection Elite, and 650.00 USD for up to 21 days on the Collective Total Protection
Concierge plan. The three pass plans carry 0.00 USD a day and 0 days.

**On the qualifying periods.** The medical qualifying period is the longest on Season Pass Protection Basic at
14 consecutive days and the shortest on the Collective Total Protection Concierge plan at 3 consecutive days;
a certificate of 13 consecutive days does not reach the Basic period while one of 14 consecutive days does.
The closure period stands at 7 consecutive days on Season Pass Protection Premier, 5 on Collective Trip
Protection Elite and 3 on the Collective Total Protection Concierge plan, and at 0 on the three plans whose
schedule of insured perils does not name mountain closure.
